prompt: Some people think that parents should teach their children how to be good members of society. Others, however, believe that school is the best place to learn this. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
intro_note: Band 7 rewrite of W7 (6.0). Keeps your position, your four-paragraph structure and your Korea example — the example is re-aimed at the claim it actually proves. Highlights mark what moves each criterion.

spans.text: Opinion is divided over whether the responsibility for
teaching children to behave well in society

highlight.label: Infinitive complement
highlight.explanation: *teach* takes a to-infinitive. This replaces the recurring "educate students how to socialize", which appeared three times in W7 and again in W3.

spans.text: rests primarily with their families or with their schools.
Although classroom life clearly offers valuable practice,

highlight.explanation: Concedes the other side before stating the position, so the introduction is not one-sided.

spans.text: I would argue that parents remain better placed to shape social behaviour

highlight.label: Position stated in the introduction
highlight.explanation: A clear position, framed as effectiveness ("better placed") rather than duty — which is what Body 2 actually argues.

spans.text: , because they can adapt their guidance to the individual child.
There is a strong case for the school.

highlight.label: Short topic sentence
highlight.explanation: A five-word claim opens the paragraph, instead of a 30-40 word formulaic frame.

highlight.label: Concrete social behaviours
highlight.explanation: W3's feedback asked for exactly these — apologising, sharing, compromise — instead of the abstract "social norms".

highlight.explanation: Your Korea example is kept, but re-aimed: a degree and an exam demonstrate training, not skill at teaching social behaviour. The original leap — that this makes teachers better than parents — is gone.

highlight.explanation: This is the corrected fault: your Body 2 ended on teacher overwhelm, repeating Body 1. Each body needs a distinct main idea.

spans.text: In conclusion,
